claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy contains FCC and B2 phases.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 near 600°C enhances L12 ordering within its FCC domains.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 near 600°C produces jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The aging-induced ordering and boundary structure locally increase the elastic modulus.
Enhanced ordering increases the activation barrier for cross-slip.
An increased cross-slip barrier promotes planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries act as stress concentrators and promote crack initiation.
At approximately 600°C, ordering and phase-boundary stress concentration are maximized, causing plastic instability and brittle fracture under mechanical loading.
Aging near 750°C reduces ordering relative to the state aged near 600°C.
Aging near 750°C forms more ductile or smoother transition zones along B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The transition zones formed near 750°C relieve phase-boundary stress concentrations and restore ductility or toughness.
The alloy exhibits a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response as aging temperature increases.
The approximately 600°C-aged alloy has significantly lower toughness and ductility than the approximately 750°C-aged alloy.
Below approximately 550°C, no significant ductile-brittle transition occurs.
Brittle behavior occurs between approximately 550°C and 750°C.
Conventional-alloy embrittlement typically arises from grain-boundary impurity segregation rather than intrinsic ordering and phase-boundary effects.
Using a controlled atmosphere avoids external impurity-segregation effects during aging.

contradictions.description: The boundary field says brittle behavior persists between approximately 550°C and 750°C and recovery occurs beyond 750°C, whereas the predicted outcome and mechanism say the alloy aged at approximately 750°C already has recovered ductility.
